## Exercises

1.  Create a new age variable called `age_cat` that categorizes `age` into a factor with the following categories (Hint: Be mindful of any missing data):

    -   \< 30
    -   30-39
    -   40-49
    -   50-59
    -   60-69
    -   70 +




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
gss_cat_newage<-gss_cat %>% 
  mutate(age_cat = case_when(age < 30 ~ "< 30",
                             between(age, 30, 39) ~ "30-39",
                             between(age, 40, 49) ~ "40-49",
                             between(age, 50, 59) ~ "50-59",
                             between(age, 60, 69) ~ "60-69",
                             age >= 70 ~ "70+",
                             TRUE ~ "-99"),
         age_cat = factor(age_cat))

levels(gss_cat_newage$age_cat)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "-99"   "< 30"  "30-39" "40-49" "50-59" "60-69" "70+"  
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}

  ggplot(aes(x = age_cat, y = age)) +
  geom_point()
```

2.  In the `relig` variable there are missing data not showing as `NA`.  Recode these to our usual -99 and -98 values to these options.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
gss_cat_newrelig<-gss_cat %>% 
  mutate(relig2 = fct_recode(relig, 
                             "-99" = "No answer", 
                             "-98" = "Don't know"))

gss_cat_newrelig %>% 
  count(relig, relig2)
```

3. Create a new religion variable called `relig_other` that combines answers with \<100 responses into the `Other` category.  (Hint: Be mindful our the missing data you just recoded)




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
gss_cat_religoth<-gss_cat_newrelig %>% 
  mutate(relig_other = fct_other(relig2, 
                                 drop = c("Native american",
                                          "Other eastern",
                                          "Hinduism",
                                          "Orthodox-christian")))

gss_cat_religoth %>% 
  count(relig_other, relig2)
```

birthdays_dt<-birthdays %>% 
  mutate(birthday = ymd(glue("{birth_year} {birth_month} {birth_day}")))

3. What is the average age of this population as of today? (Hint: use `today()` and `time_length()`)




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
birthdays_dt %>% 
  mutate(age = time_length(today()-birthday,unit = "years")) %>% 
  summarize(avg_age = mean(age, na.rm=TRUE))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 1 × 1
  avg_age
    <dbl>
1    52.3
```


:::
:::




4. What is the average age of enrollment by sex? (Hint: use `time_length()`)




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
birthdays_dt %>% 
  mutate(age_enrollment = time_length(enrollment_date-birthday,unit = "years")) %>% 
  group_by(sex) %>% 
  summarize(avg_age_enrollment = mean(age_enrollment, na.rm=TRUE))
```
